slug: 2024-01-01 CRVS Systems - Burkina Faso civil registration technical brief

facts.fact: The brief says a new one-step digital birth registration system, iCivil, was introduced in 2018 in a limited number of health facilities and piloted through 2018 and 2019, with 908 and 1,505 notifications received in those two years.
The brief's table shows 9,638 births notified and recorded through iCivil from January to August 2020 and no deaths, and it states that death registration has yet to be rolled out.

The brief says that in 2020, in municipalities using iCivil, maternity staff registered births by smartphone from the health facility directly to the national server at DGMEC, where they are entered in the National Register of Civil Status, and the civil status centre prints the certificate from that register.
The brief says iCivil became fully operational in 2020 after piloting in 2018 and 2019, and that the number of iCivil-enabled registration points and of births registered through it rose during 2020.
The brief says that as of January 2021 only 50 of 2,584 vital event notification points across the country use the iCivil system.

The brief elsewhere says there are 1,193 civil status offices and 2,584 registration points and that so far only 130 registration points use iCivil (104 in health facilities and 16 in local communities, its own breakdown, which sums to 120); it gives no date for this count, so it is dated to the latest date in the brief's text, January 2021, and it disagrees with the brief's other figure of 50.

The brief says the government bought the licence for iCivil from the private company that developed it and now owns the system, that DGMEC under the Ministry of Territorial Administration adopted it in 2019 and operates the national digital register, and that civil registration centres using it fall under DGMEC and health centres under the Ministry of Health; undated, so dated to the latest date in the brief's text.

The brief says the government is further deploying iCivil with support from financial and technical partners such as UNFPA, and names no domestic budget line (it gives an annual mobile data cost of 1,200,000 CFA without saying who pays); undated, so dated to the latest date in the brief's text.

systems.platform: iCivil (bubble-seal bracelet, smartphone application, encrypted SMS to a central server)
systems.owner: DGMEC, Ministry of Territorial Administration, Decentralization and Social Cohesion; licence bought by the government from a private company
systems.tiers: health facility maternities and some local communities as registration points; civil status centres issue certificates; central server and National Register of Civil Status at DGMEC headquarters

note: Read from the artefact PDF. Ten pages, undated; its latest internal date is January 2021, used where a statement carries no date. The two office counts (50 and 130 of 2,584 points) disagree and both are recorded. Not recorded as facts: the paper register in duplicate, which the brief gives as the legal procedure; the statement that the law recognises only paper registers and a revision of the Code is in draft; interoperability with the identity office and others, given as planned. iCivil assigns a unique identification number at birth. VENEEM is not named in the PDF.
